papers.title: Using the aperiodic slope across learning to predict sleep-based memory consolidation
papers.summary: Participants (n=27) learned object-word pairs before a nap or wake interval, with resting-state EEG used to derive aperiodic slope changes and a delayed recognition task assessing memory and N400 amplitude. A shift toward inhibition during learning predicted better memory accuracy only in the nap condition, and homeostatic renormalisation (inhibition across sleep) predicted reduced N400 amplitudes, linking synaptic homeostatic processes to memory consolidation.

papers.title: PADA: perturbation-aware differential Riemannian attention for robust motor imagery decoding.
papers.summary: The authors introduced PADA, a perturbation-aware differential Riemannian attention mechanism for EEG-based motor imagery decoding, using learnable Riemannian mapping and tangent-space perturbations to suppress noise-sensitive attention. PADA achieved 81.44% and 92.79% clean-condition accuracy on BCI Competition IV-2a and Zhou2016, dropped only 12% under 50% noise, and reached 70.46% binary accuracy on hand motor imagery with 12 training samples in 227 subjects.

papers.title: Revisiting post-stimulus theta activity: evidence for a broadband rather than narrowband spectral origin.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: Using high-density EEG during audiovisual simple reaction-time and visual oddball tasks in children, the study compared conventional time-frequency analyses with analyses that explicitly modeled and removed aperiodic 1/f activity. Stimulus onset robustly increased aperiodic exponent and offset; after accounting for aperiodic activity, apparent theta increases were largely abolished and beta desynchronization was overestimated, while alpha desynchronization remained robust.

papers.title: How auditory rhythm perception shapes speech production: The influence of neural synchronization and rhythmic patterns.
papers.summary: Eighty-six Mandarin speakers performed speech production of [2+2] and [1+3] rhythmic patterns after congruent or incongruent pure-tone primes, with neural synchronization quantified via cerebral-acoustic coherence (CACoh) between EEG and prime envelopes. A Group × Target Type interaction showed low synchronizers had reliable priming for [1+3] targets while high synchronizers showed little priming, and higher theta-band CACoh predicted smaller priming effects for [1+3] targets.

papers.title: LTPat-based SOXFE: A self-organized explainable feature engineering model for automated fibromyalgia detection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: This study evaluated a self-organized explainable feature engineering (SOXFE) model using LTPat feature extraction, CWNCA selection, tkNN classification, and DLob explanation for EEG-based fibromyalgia detection from sleep EEG in NREM stage 2 and stage 3. Record-wise LORO yielded held-out-epoch accuracy of 92.77% for stage 2 and 97.00% for stage 3, but participant linkage was unavailable, so person-independent performance may be overestimated.

papers.title: Gravity-awareness: a deep learning and LLM framework for predicting human adaptation to altered gravitational environments.
papers.summary: The study presents a computational framework (CorticalG and PhysioG) trained on parabolic flight data to predict neurophysiological adaptation to altered gravity, and uses the LLM Claude 3.5 Sonnet to generate narratives of subjective experience across gravity conditions. The framework offers a predictive tool for assessing human performance and resilience in spaceflight.

papers.title: Comparing Maximally Collapsing Metric Learning and Optimized Tunable Q-Wavelet Transform for Schizophrenia Identification Using EEG Signals.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
papers.summary: The study compared a transformer based on Maximally Collapsing Metric Learning (MCML) with optimized Tunable Q-Wavelet Transform (TQWT) for classifying schizophrenia from EEG signals using eight nonlinear features and three classifiers. MCML achieved 100% accuracy with a single electrode channel, outperforming TQWT and other classifiers which reached up to 99.94%.

papers.title: What drives intersubject correlation of EEG during auditory narratives?
papers.summary: The study investigated the drivers of intersubject correlation (ISC) of EEG during auditory narratives using temporal response functions (TRFs) and correlated component analysis. Acoustic features explained more variance and were main contributors to ISC, while word surprisal affected ISC only during active engagement, and linear responses accounted for only a small fraction of ISC, suggesting nonlinear responses dominate.

papers.title: Variability in Preprocessing and Analysis of the Error-Related Negativity in Adult Response-Conflict Studies: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of 202 adult response-conflict studies from 1995–2025 found highly heterogeneous preprocessing and analysis pipelines for the error-related negativity (ERN), with no two studies using the same workflow and persistent reporting gaps. Analytic decisions showed modest temporal shifts but high overall diversity, sample sizes remained insufficient for typical effects, and preregistrations were extremely rare.

papers.title: Towards a Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) for Improving Phonological Processing in Developmental Dyslexia: An Exploratory Study.
papers.summary: An exploratory study developed an EEG-based brain-computer interface (BCI) aimed at improving phonological processing in developmental dyslexia, tested with adults with and without dyslexia over 16 sessions. Offline BCI learning scores were significantly associated with improvements in non-word reading, real word reading, and amplitude rise time discrimination, interpreted within Temporal Sampling theory.

papers.title: Exploratory analysis of electroencephalogram activity preceding nocturnal enuresis episodes using home-based sleep monitoring.
papers.summary: This exploratory study analyzed EEG spectral power immediately before nocturnal enuresis episodes in 18 children using home-based single-channel EEG. Delta-band power was significantly higher on wet nights at 10 and 5 minutes before onset compared to dry nights, suggesting transient sleep deepening preceding enuresis.

papers.title: Distinct brain network organization in asynchronous and synchronous motor observation and motor imagery: evidence from EEG functional connectivity, phase-amplitude coupling, and decoding.
papers.summary: The study compared asynchronous and synchronous motor observation and motor imagery (MOMI) during a basketball set-shot task using EEG functional connectivity, phase-amplitude coupling, and decoding. Results showed distinct network patterns: asynchronous MOMI had sustained alpha connectivity and stronger theta-phase coupling, and achieved the highest decoding accuracy (79.41%), indicating temporal organization shapes brain network dynamics.

papers.title: Neural Oscillatory and Sympathetic Arousal Dynamics During Mindfulness Meditation: Characterizing Relaxed Alertness.
papers.summary: The study examined EEG oscillations and skin conductance level (SCL) during brief breath-focused mindfulness meditation to characterize relaxed alertness. Meditation was associated with greater theta amplitude and exploratory delta increases, while alpha showed no reliable effects and SCL showed an initial decrease followed by a later increase; global alpha was positively associated with SCL during meditation.

papers.title: Lateralized amyloid PET uptake and beta-band connectivity in relation to cognition in temporal lobe epilepsy.
papers.summary: In 30 adults with mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, focus-relative amyloid PET uptake (18F-florapronol) was associated with beta-band EEG connectivity and cognitive processing speed. Ipsilateral medial temporal SUVR correlated with inter-hemispheric beta wPLI (ρ=0.617, q=0.034), but indirect associations with processing speed were exploratory and did not survive correction.

papers.title: LIBPhys-EGG: An open-access multichannel electrogastrography and accelerometry dataset for reproducible research in gastrointestinal electrophysiology.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors present LIBPhys-EGG, an open-access dataset of multichannel electrogastrography and tri-axial accelerometry from 15 healthy adults (30 sessions, 111.8 h). Benchmark analyses showed strong post-prandial changes and a Random Forest classifier distinguishing pre- vs. post-prandial states with 0.93 accuracy and 0.966 AUC-ROC on recording-level splits.

papers.title: Pain Enhances the Auditory P2 but Attenuates Mismatch Response and P3a.
papers.summary: Using a three-stimulus auditory oddball paradigm and EEG, the study examined how tonic thermal pain modulates auditory event-related potentials. Compared to baseline and warmth, pain enhanced early P2 responses and reduced mismatch negativity and P3a amplitudes, without significant behavioral differences.

papers.title: High Doses of N-Acetyl-P-Aminophenol Cause Acute Changes in Electroencephalographic and Electrocardiographic Activities in Wistar Rats.
authors: Luiz Gustavo Dos Reis de Freitas
papers.summary: In Wistar rats, a toxic oral dose of N-acetyl-p-aminophenol (1 g/kg) reduced delta, theta, beta, and gamma EEG wave activity while increasing alpha activity, with synchronous reduced cardiac electrical activity. Liver enzymes significantly increased during 12-hour follow-up, indicating early brain and heart electrical changes independent of liver damage.

papers.title: Complementing Engel Classification: Postoperative Scalp EEG as an Objective Indicator in SEEG-Guided Radiofrequency Thermocoagulation-A Seizure-Onset Pattern-Based Stratified Analysis.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 25 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy treated with SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation, low-voltage fast activity (LVFA)-present seizure-onset patterns were strongly associated with seizure freedom (92.3% vs. 33.3%, p=0.004) and postoperative scalp EEG normalization (87.5% vs. 33.3%, p=0.028). Postoperative EEG normalization complemented Engel classification as an objective outcome indicator.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiac Electrophysiology Ethics, Explainability, Equity, and the Road Ahead.
papers.summary: This review discusses ethical, practical, and regulatory challenges of artificial intelligence in cardiac electrophysiology, including dataset bias, explainability, equity, and accountability. It outlines strategies for transparency and highlights future directions such as digital twins, multimodal risk engines, and real-time procedural guidance.

papers.title: Subjective experience of listening to favorite songs and Murottal Al-Qur'an in young adult women: a quantitative EEG case series.
papers.summary: A case series of four young adult women compared alpha-band EEG power during listening to favorite songs and Qur'anic murottal with an eyes-closed baseline. Individual alpha event-related desynchronization/synchronization topography broadly aligned with self-reported mental states (relaxation, visual imagery, concentration) during both conditions, with notable between-subject variability.

papers.title: Cost-Effective Ultrathin SEBS-Ag Electrodes of Substrate-Regulated Microcracks for Robust Skin Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: The study developed an ultrathin stretchable silver-based electrode by tuning polymer substrate stiffness and polarity, achieving a 7.6 µm electrode with skin-mimetic modulus (1.35 MPa) and low sheet resistance (9.26 Ω/sq). The electrode enabled low-artifact ECG monitoring over 24 h and maintained high signal-to-noise ratio (29.27 dB) during 13 km/h running, outperforming commercial Ag/AgCl electrodes.

papers.title: Temporal profile of serum orexin-A in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a prospective longitudinal study.
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal observational study measured serum orexin-A at 6-12 and 72-96 hours in 41 neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), comparing those treated with therapeutic hypothermia (TH) to those without. Orexin-A trajectories differed significantly: levels were preserved or increased under TH but declined without it, and the change correlated with amplitude-integrated EEG background but not with injury markers.

papers.title: Cell Village Captures Populational Heterogeneity of Sunitinib Cardiotoxicity.
papers.summary: Using the Cell Village platform with iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from 20 donors, this study linked pooled single-nucleus RNA sequencing with functional phenotyping to reveal interindividual heterogeneity in sunitinib cardiotoxicity. Relaxation velocity best correlated with toxicity severity, and gene modules for calcium handling and structural organization were associated with donor-specific toxicity and recovery, with tocotrienol producing partial donor-dependent improvement.

papers.title: Exploring the Neural Mechanisms of Acupuncture Stimulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Multimodal Neuroimaging Trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized, sham-controlled, multimodal neuroimaging trial to investigate acute neural mechanisms of acupuncture in autism spectrum disorder and typically developing individuals, using fNIRS and EEG before and after verum or sham acupuncture. The primary outcome is differences in resting-state network metrics and frontal relative band power by disease status.

papers.title: Advantage of cerebellar intermittent theta-burst stimulation in Alzheimer's disease (ACT-AD): study protocol for a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
papers.summary: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial protocol will test long-term neuronavigated cerebellar intermittent theta-burst stimulation in 100 patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease, with the primary outcome being change in CDR-SB from baseline to week 12. Exploratory outcomes include EEG, blood biomarkers, and MRI.

papers.title: Multimodal ophthalmic findings in patients with mucopolysaccharidosis: A prospective observational study.
papers.summary: This prospective observational study characterized ocular involvement in 22 pediatric patients with mucopolysaccharidosis using multimodal structural and functional assessments, finding that corneal opacity was the predominant manifestation and correlated strongly with corneal densitometry. Multimodal testing also revealed elevated intraocular pressure in four MPS VI patients and electrophysiological abnormalities in nine of 14 tested patients.

papers.title: A histidine-mediated supramolecular mechanism links temperature and pH activation of the sperm channel CatSper.
papers.summary: Combining comparative genomics across 47 species, AlphaFold3 modeling, and functional experiments in mouse sperm, this study proposes a histidine-mediated supramolecular mechanism in which temperature-dependent deprotonation of CatSper1 histidine clusters couples neighboring CatSper complexes to promote synchronized channel activation. Partial removal of the CatSper1 N-terminus selectively impaired temperature-dependent activation.

papers.title: A Rounding Error Dressed as Reform: The Implications of a Large Private Health Insurance Company's Prior Authorization Concession for the Electrophysiology Patient.
papers.summary: This commentary examines the implications of a large private health insurance company's prior authorization concession for electrophysiology patients, framing it as a minor change rather than meaningful reform and discussing consequences for access to implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, pacemakers, and related care.

papers.title: Alexander Disease Diagnosed in an Obstetrics Patient: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
papers.summary: This case report describes the first peripartum onset of adult-onset Alexander disease type II in a 33-year-old woman who presented with neuropsychiatric symptoms mimicking posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and was diagnosed via a pathogenic GFAP variant (Arg79Leu). The patient improved with rehabilitation but had residual dysarthria at 2-month follow-up, highlighting the need to consider adult-onset neurogenetic disorders in atypical peripartum neurological presentations.

papers.title: Human Th17 state classification reveals a selective vulnerability in acylcarnitine metabolism in type 2 diabetes
papers.summary: The authors developed a nanovial-based single-cell ELISA to isolate cytokine-secreting human Th17 cells and define transcriptional signatures of non-pathogenic versus pathogenic Th17 states. Applying these tools with metabolic modeling revealed that Th17np cells predominate in type 2 diabetes and exhibit impaired fatty acid oxidation despite elevated CPT1A, identifying acylcarnitine metabolism as a regulator of Th17 state balance and a selective metabolic vulnerability in type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Refractory Status Epilepticus Following Erroneous Intrathecal Injection of Tranexamic Acid: A Case Report and Long-Term Follow-Up and Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 32-year-old man who developed refractory myoclonic status epilepticus and rhabdomyolysis after erroneous intrathecal injection of 300 mg tranexamic acid during saphenous vein stripping. Despite recovery without immediate neurological deficit, he developed persistent cognitive impairment and posttraumatic stress disorder, underscoring the severe neurotoxicity of intrathecal tranexamic acid and the need for long-term multidisciplinary follow-up.

papers.title: PKD2 structural destabilization drives primary cilia degeneration and ADPKD pathogenicity.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using cryo-EM, primary cilia electrophysiology, super-resolution imaging, and a novel mouse model, this study showed that the ADPKD-associated PKD2 variant D511V destabilizes the channel's voltage sensor domain, abolishing ciliary trafficking and function and causing renal tubule primary cilia degeneration and rapid renal cysts. These findings establish a direct link between in vitro molecular dysfunction and in vivo pathogenicity and provide a new tool for evaluating ADPKD therapies.

papers.title: Neuronal IL-18 Signaling in the Medial Habenula Contributes to Schizophrenia-Like Behavioral Deficits via ERK-Associated BDNF Suppression.
papers.summary: Using an MK-801-treated rat model, this study found that neuronal IL-18 in the medial habenula is a predominant pathological signal driving schizophrenia-like behavioral deficits via ERK overactivation, reduced BDNF expression, and neuronal hypoactivity. Neuron-specific IL-18 overexpression induced schizophrenia-like behaviors, while knockdown or ERK inhibition ameliorated molecular, cellular, and behavioral deficits.

papers.title: In Situ ATR-FTIR Analysis of Nalidixic Acid Degradation upon Oxygenation of Fe(II)-Sorbed Ferrihydrite and Maghemite Surfaces.
papers.summary: In situ ATR-FTIR spectroscopy showed that oxygenating Fe(II)-sorbed ferrihydrite and maghemite triggers abiotic degradation of nalidixic acid within hours, without light or added strong oxidants. Mineral-dependent product fates were observed, with maghemite causing pyridinic ring cleavage while ferrihydrite produced a slightly different end-product signal.

papers.title: Hyperactive Delirium Temporally Associated With Hydroxyzine in a Child With Succinic Semialdehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency Presenting With Psychotic Symptoms: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 12-year-old girl with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) who presented with psychotic symptoms and developed hyperactive delirium temporally associated with hydroxyzine administration. Symptoms improved after hydroxyzine discontinuation and initiation of low-dose quetiapine with environmental interventions, though multiple contributing factors were present.

papers.title: An AI-Enabled Translational Drug Discovery Framework for NALCN Channelopathy: From High-Throughput Screening to Therapeutic Candidate
papers.summary: An AI-enabled translational drug discovery framework combined phenotypic high-throughput screening, Boltz-2 structural modeling, and experimental validation to identify NALCN inhibitors for CLIFAHDD. Aprepitant emerged as a lead candidate, showing partial inhibition of NALCN currents in HEK293 cells (IC50 ~2.22 µM), reducing sodium leak currents in mouse hippocampal neurons, and rescuing hyperlocomotor and dystonic phenotypes in a C. elegans gain-of-function model.

papers.title: A membrane-disruptive action of VBIT-4 challenges its role as a widely used VDAC1 oligomerization inhibitor.
papers.summary: High-speed AFM, electrophysiology, microscale thermophoresis, and molecular dynamics showed that VBIT-4 disrupts lipid membranes and increases permeability independently of VDAC1, without altering VDAC1 channel properties or oligomerization. VBIT-4 also induced VDAC1-independent cytotoxicity in HeLa cells above 10 µM, challenging its use as a specific VDAC1 oligomerization inhibitor.

papers.title: Structure-activity relationships of BnOCPA derivatives at native pre- and postsynaptic adenosine A1Rs.
papers.summary: Tested four BnOCPA derivatives (MBnOCPA, PhOCPA, BPhOCPA) for pre- vs postsynaptic adenosine A1R selectivity in rat hippocampus. All inhibited CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission presynaptically without hyperpolarizing CA1 neurons at inhibitory concentrations, and BPhOCPA showed no postsynaptic hyperpolarization up to 10 µM, indicating structural modifications can tune discrimination between native A1R populations.

papers.title: Multiomics Insights Linking Personal Care Products Exposure to Serum Lipid Profiles in Older Adults: The China BAPE Study.
papers.summary: A five-wave prospective panel study of 76 healthy older adults in China integrated urinary personal care product biomarkers with transcriptomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics. Four PCPs (BP-2, BP-3, 4-OHBP, EtP) were associated with altered serum lipid profiles, converging on a PPAR-centered immunometabolic network with S100 signaling and links to inflammatory, oxidative stress, and ECG changes.

papers.title: Clinically Probable Guillain-Barré Syndrome and Herpesvirus-Associated Syndromes in Advanced Untreated HIV: A Retrospective Case Cluster from India.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Association of Providers of AIDS Care
papers.summary: Retrospective review of adults with advanced untreated HIV presenting with acute symmetrical weakness at an Indian HIV specialty centre in 2019-2020; eight of 139 admissions met Brighton level 3 clinically probable GBS. All eight had concurrent infections, including herpesvirus-associated syndromes, and seven recovered after multimodal treatment while one died.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
